arch_ahsReceptionCentres: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: Reception Centres: A Guide for Municipalities, Alberta Health Services (Safe Healthy Environments), PUB-0539-202405 (c)2020: ~3.5 m2 per person, up to 9 m2 for wheelchair users/service animals/assistance (p. 4); sleeping >=3.5 m2/person, ~1 m between cots (p. 6); 1 toilet per 20-25 people, final by AHJ under Alberta Building Code (p. 5); ~2 L/person/day drinking, 7.5-12 L with food and hygiene (p. 4); indoor 19-22 C (p. 4) — https://www.albertahealthservices.ca/assets/wf/eph/wf-eph-reception-centres-municipalities.pdf
arch_unhcrShelterStandards: DESIGN GUIDE (intl. benchmark): Emergency Shelter Solutions and Standards, UNHCR Emergency Handbook, 21 Jan 2026: covered living space 3.5 m2/person (warm climate, excl. cooking); 4.5-5.5 m2/person indoor (cold climate); cites Sphere 2018 as minimum standards — https://emergency.unhcr.org/print/pdf/node/538
arch_hcCleanerAirSpaces: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: Guidance for Cleaner Air Spaces during Wildfire Smoke Events, Health Canada, Sept 2020 (mod. 13 Nov 2020): 'A MERV value of 13 or more is recommended'; portable cleaner CADR (smoke) 2-3 x room volume per hour; temp below 26 C, CO <10 ppm, CO2 <1000 ppm, RH 35-50%; connected to emergency power, generators away and downwind of intakes; staging entryway; occupancy set beforehand per ASHRAE 62.1-2019 (no m2/person); water/washrooms out of scope — https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/publications/healthy-living/guidance-cleaner-air-spaces-during-wildfire-smoke-events.html
arch_vchCoolingSpaces: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: Creating Cooling Spaces During Hot Weather: Guidance for Community Organizations, Vancouver Coastal Health, 6 Jun 2023: 'keep spaces at or below 26°C' (p. 5); accessible washrooms, drinking water (p. 5); 'Maximize air flow and filtration' (p. 7); no m2/person or capacity — https://prod-careers.vch.ca/en/media/19776
arch_covHeatMemo2025: GOVERNMENT: Overview of Extreme Heat Plans and Actions 2025, memo S. Singh (DCM) to Mayor and Council, City of Vancouver, 3 Jul 2025: 39 civic facilities (19 community centres, 20 libraries) as cooling centres (p. 3, App. Table 1 p. 6); 14 cleaner air spaces at community centres and libraries with high-performance filtration (p. 5); no capacities — https://vancouver.ca/files/cov/2025-07-03-memo-extreme-heat-plans-summer-2025.pdf
arch_covFiltrationStudy: CONSULTANT REPORT FOR CITY: Filtration Study for the City of Vancouver, Final Report, Integral Group for City of Vancouver, 10 Nov 2021: 'MERV 13 is the starting minimum filtration efficiency stipulated for all new Part 3 and Part 9 buildings' (p. 2); wildfire areas target MERV 16 (p. 2); WHO 4-6 ACH (p. 9) — https://vancouver.ca/files/cov/filtration-best-practices-study.pdf
arch_bcHarsVch: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: Heat Plan: Long-Term Care/Assisted Living, Overview and Completion Guide, hosted by Vancouver Coastal Health (issuer not named), Apr 2025, quoting BC HEAT HARS criteria: Southwest heat warning >=29 C day and >=16 C night, 2+ days; extreme heat emergency >=31 C rising 3+ days (pp. 3-4); cooling zones at 26 C (p. 9) — https://prod-careers.vch.ca/en/media/14146
arch_edmExtremeWeather: GOVERNMENT: Extreme Weather Response Summary, City of Edmonton (Policy C620, with Homeward Trust), Mar 2025: cold activation -20 C with wind chill 3+ days; heat 29 C day and >=14 C night 3+ days; AQHI >=7 2+ days; up to 50 overnight spaces (Al Rashid Mosque); recreation centres and libraries as respite, no capacities — https://www.gov.edmonton.ab.ca/sites/default/files/public-files/assets/PDF/Extreme-Weather-Overview-2019-2025.pdf
arch_essProgramGuide2025: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: Emergency Support Services (ESS) Program Guide, BC EMCR (issuer inferred), 2025: no m2/person or washroom ratios found in first 100k of 121k chars; 'prepare potential reception centres and group lodging facilities' (p. 7) — https://ess.gov.bc.ca/app/uploads/sites/931/2025/12/ESS-Program-Guide-2025-2.pdf
